subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 13 updates

question: Can a workflow/security owner approve the final pinned action revisions after confirming that GitHub App token, registry-login, CodeQL upload, and Codex-action privilege contracts remain appropriate for the latest head?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes third-party executable code on workflows with secrets and elevated repository capabilities; this requires repository-specific risk acceptance rather than an automated repair choice.

options.title: Audit and merge after final proof
options.body: Review the final action revisions and accept the update once a redacted final-head workflow result demonstrates the privileged paths complete as expected.

options.title: Split the sensitive updates
options.body: Separate token-minting and Codex-action changes from lower-risk setup and stale-management updates if reviewers want narrower security review units.

options.title: Pause this roll-up
options.body: Leave the PR open until the security/workflow owner can review the upstream action contracts and final workflow evidence.

recommendation.title: Audit and merge after final proof
recommendation.body: Review the final action revisions and accept the update once a redacted final-head workflow result demonstrates the privileged paths complete as expected.

likelyOwner.reason: The release-path ownership evidence is the strongest available routing signal for the Docker and release workflow portion of this cross-workflow update.
